chapter: The Famous Door, Billy May and the Palomar fire
title: Playing Ellington's tunes, not his arrangements
summary: Barnet says the band played Ellington compositions in its own arrangements, as Duke wrote in Music Is My Mistress.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: I've read a lot of references to your band's material in which it says you played a lot of Duke's arrangements, but you played very few of Duke's actual
No, we didn't play his arrangements. We played his tunes.

Yeah, because as Duke says, in, "Music is My Mistress," he said, "Charlie Barnet has always been a wonderful friend to me, because of his musicianship, good judgment and good taste. He has always had people working for him whose potential was immense," and he mentions the people, "and at the same time he constantly bolstered my ego by playing a book almost full of our compositions. The arrangements of our things, no copycat versions, were done to fit the Charlie Barnet Band, and they were suitable for whatever occasion he played." It's as though, I feel, Duke wanted to set the record straight, because of all --
